content.title: KITCHEN FIXES FOR ANNOYING LITTLE PROBLEMS DOCTORS SAY ARE FINE TO DIY
facts: **Hiccups That Won't Quit** – Swallow 1 tsp of dry sugar, the grainy texture interrupts the nerve spasm causing the hiccup.
**Stuffy Nose at Night** – Prop your head up on 2 pillows, gravity keeps mucus from pooling and blocking airflow.
**Minor Burns** – Run it under cool (not ice-cold) water for 10 minutes, then apply plain yogurt to calm the sting.
**Bad Breath Fast** – Chew on a sprig of parsley, its chlorophyll neutralizes sulfur compounds from garlic or coffee.
**Toothache Before the Dentist** – Press a clove against the sore spot, its eugenol acts as a natural numbing agent.
**Dry, Cracked Lips** – Dab on a bit of honey before bed, it locks in moisture overnight better than most balms.
**Leg Cramp at 2 AM** – Pinch your upper lip hard for 20 seconds, it can interrupt the nerve signal causing the spasm.
**Itchy Bug Bite** – Press a warm spoon on it for 30 seconds, heat breaks down the itch-triggering compounds in the venom.
**Hoarse Voice** – Sip warm water with 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, it thins mucus coating the vocal cords.
**Follow along** – for more quick fixes like this you can actually use today.
content.caption:
A few of these are worth keeping in your back pocket. The sugar trick for hiccups works because the dry granules force your throat muscles to focus on swallowing instead of spasming, which resets the nerve causing the hiccup in the first place. The clove trick for toothaches isn't just an old wives' tale either, eugenol is a real compound with mild anesthetic properties that numbs the nerve endings around the sore tooth until you can get seen. And honey on cracked lips works because it's naturally humectant, meaning it pulls moisture in and seals it there, which is why it often outperforms store-bought balm overnight. Everyone's body reacts a little differently, so pay attention to what actually helps you.
